messages:
matt.jackson: Hey team — running a POC for ACME, demo Thurs. Hitting 413 Payload Too Large when calling POST /v1/generate with ~400k chars in the context. Error in client: "413 Request Entity Too Large". Any quick fixes? @ellie.yang @raj.patel
ellie.yang: 413 usually means a proxy/nginx limit, not model max_tokens. Can you paste the curl you used (sanitized)? Also, how big is the request body in bytes?
matt.jackson: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @payload.json (payload.json ~ 6.2MB). No gzip.
mike: 6MB should be fine for most hosted gateways but our edge/API gateway may default to 5MB. Two quick tries: 1) gzip the request body 2) switch to sending a resumable presigned upload for large blobs then reference it in the prompt.
ellie.yang: Also check model max token limit — if you send input_tokens + max_new_tokens > model_limit, the server might truncate or reject. But 413 is upstream. If you can, try: curl --compressed ... or add header Accept-Encoding: gzip and compress payload.
raj.patel: On self-hosted/on-prem we often hit nginx client_max_body_size = 1m by default. If ACME is using our private deployment or their LB, ask infra to bump to ~20M. For hosted customers we can request a per-account body limit increase (needs infra assist).
sara.sales: If we advise them to move to Dedicated to avoid gateway limits, what is the cost delta for a week-long POC? They care about cost for the demo.
ellie.yang: For short POCs we can offer a temporary Dedicated slot (small GPU pool) — ops approval required; pricing is typically monthly minimum prorated to days, rough estimate $X/day. Recommend first trying gzip or presigned upload, that’s cheapest.
raj.patel: If they want immediate unblock, @infra-bot can we increase ingress body limit for acct acme-poc by temp rule?
infra-bot: ingress-gateway: Received request to increase client_max_body_size for account "acme-poc". Applied temporary increase to 20M on edge cluster eu-west-1. Please validate within 10 minutes.
matt.jackson: Re-tested after 5m with same curl but gzip enabled — success! No truncation and response streaming started. Thanks all.
ellie.yang: Great — follow up: recommend they adopt chunking and context windowing. Share this snippet for chunking: ```python
# naive chunker
def chunk_text(s, max_chars=30000):
    return [s[i:i+max_chars] for i in range(0, len(s), max_chars)]
```
mike: Also note: streaming generation reduces memory on client and avoids single huge POSTs. For the long term, look at our SDK upload+reference flow for large docs.
sara.sales: I'll update the deal notes: ACME POC unblocked, suggested gzipping and temporary infra tweak; offer Dedicated for larger demos if they want higher throughput.
matt.jackson: Adding one last ask — do we need a security questionnaire sign-off for presigned upload flow? They asked about data retention.
ellie.yang: Presigned objects stored in object store with configurable retention and encryption. For enterprise, we can enable short TTL and KMS encryption — ops/security will need to sign off. Ping sec@sales.
matt.jackson: Perfect. Closing the loop, thanks everyone :thumbsup:
